# [TASK] Make the autonomous lock/halt check survive fresh-checkout runs

## Task
CLAUDE.md's "Before starting any work" section checked `.claude/.autonomous-lock`
and `.claude/.autonomous-halt` on local disk. But the scheduled routine's own
prompt states every firing starts from a fresh checkout — so a lock file that
only ever lived on local disk could never be seen by a later run's container.
The check always passed trivially, and the mechanism couldn't actually
prevent concurrent runs.

This wasn't theoretical: on 2026-08-04 a run closed #108 (commit `a0fd191`,
pushed ~08:35:54Z) while a second run's fresh checkout was independently
underway (no lock file present locally, because none could be — the checkout
was minutes old). Both runs proceeded without either seeing the other.

## Scope
Only the lock/halt protocol described in CLAUDE.md's "Before starting any
work" section. Not the Sprint-close merge-to-main path (the Story's other
open acceptance criterion) — that's separate, unrelated work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] CLAUDE.md's lock/halt check reads `origin/develop` (via `git fetch`
      + `git show origin/develop:.claude/...`), not local disk, since local
      disk is meaningless on a fresh checkout
- [x] Acquiring the lock commits and pushes it to `develop` immediately,
      before any other work begins, so concurrent fresh checkouts can see it
- [x] Releasing the lock (end of run, including `WIP:` handoffs) commits and
      pushes its removal
- [x] A lost race (push rejected because another run's lock commit landed
      first) is treated as "back off", not force-pushed over
- [x] Mechanism verified by simulation in this Task (fetch/show against a
      real pushed lock commit from a separate clone), since a true two-
      session race can't be forced on demand

## Estimate
**Hours:** 1 (actual: ~0.5)

## Notes
Real collision evidence: `a0fd191` landed on `origin/develop` between this run's two fetches, with no lock file ever visible to it — the exact gap #75's AC5 describes.

Fix in `f9f8add` (CLAUDE.md protocol rewrite). Verified with a real acquire/release cycle against an independent fresh clone: after the acquire push (`b7c664b`), a separate clone confirmed `git show origin/develop:.claude/.autonomous-lock` succeeded; after the release push (`057c2db`), a second clone confirmed it was gone.

Still untested: the lost-race path, where two runs attempt the acquire push in the same window and one is rejected. That needs two simultaneous sessions to exercise for real.
